source.title: LUNAR: LLM Unlearning via Neural Activation Redirection
source.authors: William F. Shen; Xin-Chi Qiu; Meghdad Kurmanji; Alexandru Iacob; Lorenzo Sani; Yi-Hong Chen; Nicola Cancedda; N. Lane

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates LUNAR against recovery attacks and reports that most tested attacks recover little or no forget-set information, while some outcomes vary by model and attack. This refines the general recovery claim with evidence for a newer counter-method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for reverse-direction activation editing, 4-bit quantization, prompt paraphrasing, and an aggregate statement about 8-bit quantization. It does not test small-set fine-tuning recovery. Layer-skip results are omitted because layer skipping is not one of the specified attack versions; LogitLens and information-extraction results do not directly test versions B–E. The table’s reference values are for LUNAR (Top-K), not a model that never saw the knowledge.
record.test_reason: The study proposes LUNAR, a new unlearning method, and attacks it with activation-direction reversal, 4-bit and 8-bit quantization, and paraphrased prompts. The results bear on whether recovery versions C, D and E hold for this method, and directly test version F (a newer method resisting attacks).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also claim robustness to layer-skip attacks when the top-K (K=3) layers are intervened on, and to LogitLens and information-extraction attacks. They attribute quantization resilience to concentrated, large updates on a single down-projection matrix.
record.recipe_differences: LUNAR redirects activations toward a model’s ignorance response and optimizes a selected MLP down-projection; it is a new method rather than a reproduction of the original unlearning methods or recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and attack type; quantization precision also matters (the reported 8-bit attack was ineffective, while 4-bit results varied).

fits_no_version.finding: In-context reintroduction lets a retrain-on-retain-set model act as if it retained forgotten knowledge. This is stated qualitatively, with no numbers and not for LUNAR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact unlearning (retraining) does not prevent in-context reintroduction of forgotten facts.

record.problems: For the attack table, the stated reference is LUNAR (Top-K), not a model that never saw the knowledge. The paper gives no uncertainty estimates. The paraphrase results are summarized with ROUGE1, which does not by itself establish whether answers were accurate or usable; for attack outcomes, the paper also relies on a broad aggregate statement for 8-bit quantization without model-specific numbers.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results for versions B–E were left out. Layer-skip results and LogitLens/information-extraction results were not extracted because they do not directly match the specified recovery operations in versions B–E.

untested.parts: The original methods (RMU, WhoIsHarryPotter, WMDP-style chance accuracy) are not tested against attacks; only baseline unlearning scores are reported.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack on LUNAR, or on the baselines.
Only the method's own unlearning vector is reversed. There is no generic refusal or ablation direction search and no deletion-versus-blocking analysis beyond LogitLens.
No per-model 8-bit values; quantization is not applied to the baselines here.
No jailbreaks, other languages or in-context reintroduction tested on LUNAR; paraphrase only, PISTOL only.
Robustness to fine-tuning relearning (version B) is untested. Attacks are run only on PISTOL and fictitious fine-tuned knowledge, not on hazardous or pretraining knowledge.

missing.what: Reverse-attack variant: the adversary knows the forget questions and computes the unlearning vector from the unlearned model. Llama2-7B forget ROUGE1 is 0.025 (no recovery).

Layer-skip attack, which bypasses the intervention layers (white-box internal edit). Forget ROUGE1 by model: Llama2 0.117, Llama3 0.180, Gemma 0.150, Qwen2 0.115, Qwen2.5 0.100, against Top-K references. Authors call this minimal recovery.
missing.locator: Table 4, §6.4 Layer skip attack, App. F.3

missing.what: LogitLens on layers 18, 19 and 32 (Llama2-7B) shows no forget-set tokens. This is internal analysis bearing on blocking versus deleting.

record.verdict_notes: All attack values are forget ROUGE1 on PISTOL only, with no uncertainty. The reference is LUNAR (Top-K), not the pre-unlearning model, so even 0.16 is far from full recovery. No fine-tuning relearning attack was run, which is the main gap for F. These are the method authors' own robustness tests; baselines were not attacked here.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not compare targeted accuracy to chance; its unlearning metrics are ROUGE-based and it does not test the full version A claim.
No recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or subset relearning examples is tested.
Tests subtracting the known LUNAR unlearning vector from activations; does not test a general activation-direction ablation or establish whether knowledge was deleted versus access-blocked.
Reports 4-bit results by model and an aggregate statement for 8-bit; does not provide model-specific 8-bit values.
Tests paraphrased prompts; does not test jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
Tests robustness to the attack types reported in this study, not every attack named in the broader claim.

relation.reason: The paper runs reverse-direction, quantization and paraphrase attacks on its own method.

tranche.reason: The study gives results that the recovery versions fail or are partial for its method. Reverse-direction, 4-bit/8-bit quantization (reproduced from [60]) and paraphrase attacks leave forget ROUGE1 near zero on most models. The authors explicitly contrast this with the larger quantization recovery [60] reported for GA/NPO, so versions C-E need restating as method-dependent.

source_check.notes: All Table 4 references are LUNAR Top-K (K=3), not the pre-unlearning model. The Table 4 reverse attack subtracts the exact unlearning vectors from the unlearning process. A variant that computes the UV from the unlearned model gives ROUGE1 0.025 on 'Llama-7B' (text only). Layer-skip results (0.100-0.180) and the LogitLens and extraction attacks (Tables 15-16) have no rows. These are the authors' own tests of their own method; no code is linked.

statements.correction: Table 4 reverse attack: the attacker knows the layer selection and the exact UVs used in unlearning and subtracts them. Forget ROUGE1 is 0.000 on Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, Gemma-7B and Qwen2.5-7B. A variant that computes the UV from the unlearned model (forget questions known) gives ROUGE1 0.025 on 'Llama-7B' (text only, §6.4).
statements.problem: The differences_stated line says the paper's attacker computes the unlearning vector from the unlearned model. That describes the paper's variant attack. The Table 4 reverse attack, which gave the cited 0.000 values, uses the exact unlearning vectors from the unlearning process. Those are a diff-in-mean computed before optimization, on the pre-unlearning model.

statements.correction: Reverse-attack forget ROUGE1 is 0.000 on Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, Gemma-7B and Qwen2.5-7B, and 0.012 to 0.160 on Qwen2-7B. All models are 7-8B. The paper does not explain the Qwen2-7B value.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the item is filed under 'Model family and size'. Within this study the outlier is Qwen2-7B. Qwen2.5-7B is the same family and the same size and gives 0.000, so the data show no family or size effect.
For this study the item only says ablation fails under LUNAR's reverse attack. That fits: 0.000 on four of five models, and Qwen2-7B rises to 0.160.
For this study it only cites r11 (8-bit stated ineffective, no numbers). That fits 'mostly does not recover'.

statements.correction: 4-bit forget ROUGE1: Llama2-7B 0.007 to 0.167 (authors say marginally effective and model non-usable); Llama3-8B 0.070 to 0.123 (no comment in the text); Gemma-7B 0.060 to 0.060; Qwen2-7B 0.012 to 0.000; Qwen2.5-7B 0.183 to 0.000. 8-bit is stated ineffective.
statements.problem: The numbers are right. But the authors call the 4-bit rise 'marginal' with the model 'non-usable' only for Llama2-7B. The text does not discuss Llama3-8B's 4-bit value, so 'outputs stay unusable' for Llama3-8B is not stated. The Llama cells are partial rises inside an item labelled challenges.

The item does not describe LUNAR but cites r12 and r13. These fit 'recover nothing': paraphrase ROUGE1 is 0.019 (Llama2-7B, reference 0.007) and 0.031 (Llama3-8B, reference 0.070), and the authors say paraphrases fail.

statements.correction: The cited reverse-attack results cover four models (Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, Gemma-7B, Qwen2.5-7B) from three families (Llama, Gemma, Qwen). The study as a whole has five models in those three families. NeurIPS 2025; no code link in the text.
statements.problem: The numbers and the Top-K reference caveat are right. The 'why' line says LUNAR is 'on four families'. The study uses five models (Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, Gemma-7B, Qwen2-7B, Qwen2.5-7B) from three families.
The text never names LUNAR, but the r4 citation fits the claim. Qwen2-7B reverse-attack forget ROUGE1 rises 0.012 to 0.160, a partial recovery, though the authors call the attack ineffective overall.
For this study it only cites r6, r7 and r11 (4-bit: Llama2-7B 0.007 to 0.167, Llama3-8B 0.070 to 0.123; 8-bit stated ineffective). These fit a bit-width factor.
